messages:
mara: FYI noticed a small but consistent increase in billed tokens during the canary. pattern looks like resume + truncated-chunk after preempted pod reroute.

hugo: short version?

mara: client opens stream -> pod preempt -> router reroutes to new pod -> client reconnects using same resume_token -> first pod had truncated mid-chunk and left provisional tokens -> ledger counts both provisional and final.

sam: resume_token equality across hops is our problem. meter keys by resume_token only so different origins collide.

ops: impact magnitude?

mara: staging saw ~1.4x tokens for affected sessions; only a handful of streams now but scales with traffic.

hugo: options: (1) change provisional key to (resume_token, hop_id) to avoid collisions, (2) emit tombstone on reroute to clear provisional on origin, (3) require authoritative session_confirm that includes resolved origin before committing billing.

sam: (1) is clean but high-cardinality and migration heavy. (2) minimal but race-prone. (3) low infra churn but UI shows provisional inflation until GC.

mara: suggestion: run a reconciler job that ingests router traces + provisional ledger and emits corrective debit events when it detects truncated fragments moved to new hop. no immediate schema change, gives telemetry.

ops: console UX: add a "reroute" badge and show provisional vs confirmed tokens per session; add filter for "reconciled adjustments".

hugo: experiment plan: enable tombstone emission for 1% traffic, reconcile job in dry-run for 100%, and hop-tagging for 0.5% to gather signals (metrics: pct_hop_mismatch, avg_provisional_ttl, double_charge_rate).

sam: set alert if double_charge_rate > 0.25% of resumed sessions.

mara: I'll prototype tombstone headers in router today and wire reconciler in staging. will post smoke results here. :thumbsup:
